# AUTO-GENERATED — TI-1415 (MCP Sentry) + TI-1417 (MCP Grafana) + TI-1428 (MCP GKE)
# Regenerado 2026-04-20
# TI-1416 (MCP Cloud Monitoring) deprecated — covered by mcp-grafana via stackdriver datasource.
# Backups: /opt/openfang.bak.20260420-185111 + docker-compose.override.yml.bak.*

services:
  # === Embedding sidecar — OpenAI-compat shim → Vertex text-embedding-005 ===
  # Replaces LiteLLM. Rotates OAuth tokens from the GCE metadata server on
  # every ~50 min and translates OpenAI /v1/embeddings into Vertex :predict.
  # OpenFang upstream has no Vertex embedding driver; this ~100-line sidecar
  # is the minimum surface to keep embeddings on Vertex without forking.
  openfang-embedding-proxy:
    image: openfang-embedding-proxy:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-embedding-proxy
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "4001"
    environment:
      VERTEX_PROJECT: prod-apps-454414
      VERTEX_REGION: us-east1
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:4001/health', timeout=3).read()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  mcp-sentry:
    image: openfang-mcp-sentry:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-sentry
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7002"
    environment:
      SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN}
      API_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${MCP_PROXY_SECRET}
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import socket; s=socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1',7002), timeout=2); s.close()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1428 — MCP GKE sidecar (replaces deprecated mcp-gcp-monitoring) ===
  mcp-gke:
    image: openfang-mcp-gke:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-gke
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7004"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:7004/healthz', timeout=3).read()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  mcp-grafana:
    image: grafana/mcp-grafana:latest
    container_name: openfang-mcp-grafana
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "8000"
    environment:
      GRAFANA_URL: https://observability.liftit.co
      GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN: ${GRAFANA_TOKEN}
    command:
      - -t
      - streamable-http
      - -address
      - 0.0.0.0:8000
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - /app/mcp-grafana
        - -h
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1430 — MCP Cloud Logging sidecar (persistent cross-service logs) ===
  mcp-logging:
    image: openfang-mcp-logging:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-logging
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7005"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen(\"http://localhost:7005/healthz\", timeout=3).read()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL


  # === TI-1431 — Slack Approver sidecar (interactive buttons + allowlist) ===
  openfang-slack-approver:
    image: openfang-slack-approver:0.1.1
    container_name: openfang-slack-approver
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - openfang
    environment:
      SLACK_APPROVER_BOT_TOKEN: ${SLACK_APPROVER_BOT_TOKEN}
      SLACK_APPROVER_APP_TOKEN: ${SLACK_APPROVER_APP_TOKEN}
      SLACK_APPROVER_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_APPROVER_CHANNEL}
      APPROVER_ALLOWLIST: ${APPROVER_ALLOWLIST}
      OPENFANG_API_BASE: http://openfang:50051
    volumes:
      - approver-state:/app/data
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1414 — MCP PostgreSQL sidecar (read-only queries) ===
  mcp-postgres:
    image: openfang-mcp-postgres:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7006"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_CONNECTION_URL: ${POSTGRES_CONNECTION_URL}
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import socket; s=socket.create_connection((\"127.0.0.1\",7006), timeout=2); s.close()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1419 — MCP GitHub sidecar (Actions + repos + PRs, read-only) ===
  mcp-github:
    image: openfang-mcp-github:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-github
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7007"
    environment:
      GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}
      GITHUB_TOOLSETS: actions,repos,pull_requests
      GITHUB_READ_ONLY: "1"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import socket; s=socket.create_connection((\"127.0.0.1\",7007), timeout=2); s.close()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1418 — Kuma trigger sidecar (polling Slack + pattern match) ===
  openfang-kuma-trigger:
    image: openfang-kuma-trigger:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-kuma-trigger
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - openfang
    environment:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}
      KUMA_CHANNEL_ID: ${KUMA_CHANNEL_ID}
      OPENFANG_AGENT_ID: assistant
      OPENFANG_API_BASE: http://openfang:50051

    volumes:
      - kuma-trigger-state:/app/data
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  openfang:
    depends_on:
      litellm:
        condition: service_healthy
      mcp-sentry:
        condition: service_healthy
      mcp-gke:
        condition: service_healthy
      mcp-grafana:
        condition: service_healthy
      mcp-logging:
        condition: service_healthy
      mcp-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      mcp-github:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      LLM_BASE_URL: http://litellm:4000/v1
      LLM_MODEL: gemini-2.5-flash
      OPENAI_API_KEY: sk-litellm-7976d848bfc488d2333573cab88bda59
      MCP_PROXY_SECRET: ${MCP_PROXY_SECRET}

"""
One-shot migration: rewrite each agent's manifest.model block so the LLM
driver uses the native OpenFang Vertex AI driver instead of going through
LiteLLM at http://litellm:4000/v1.

Before:
  [model]
  provider    = "openai"
  model       = "gemini-2.5-flash"
  api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"
  base_url    = "http://litellm:4000/v1"

After:
  [model]
  provider = "vertex-ai"
  model    = "gemini-2.5-flash"

The manifest is stored as a MessagePack BLOB in the `agents` table. Other
fields (name, description, system prompt, tools, MCP config, etc.) are
preserved unchanged.

IMPORTANT: Run with openfang kernel stopped. SQLite locking will otherwise
corrupt writes.
"""
import sqlite3
import sys

import msgpack

DB_PATH = "/data/openfang.db"

OLD_PROVIDER = "openai"
NEW_PROVIDER = "vertex-ai"
FIELDS_TO_DROP = ("api_key_env", "base_url")


def rewrite_model(model_block):
    if not isinstance(model_block, dict):
        return model_block, False
    if model_block.get("provider") != OLD_PROVIDER:
        return model_block, False
    new = dict(model_block)
    new["provider"] = NEW_PROVIDER
    for f in FIELDS_TO_DROP:
        new.pop(f, None)
    return new, True


def main():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    rows = list(conn.execute("SELECT id, name, manifest FROM agents"))
    print(f"agents in DB: {len(rows)}")
    changed = 0
    for row in rows:
        agent_id = row["id"]
        name = row["name"]
        blob = row["manifest"]
        manifest = msgpack.unpackb(blob, raw=False)
        model = manifest.get("model")
        if model is None:
            print(f"  skip name={name} reason=no_model_block")
            continue
        new_model, did = rewrite_model(model)
        if not did:
            print(f"  skip name={name} provider={model.get('provider')}")
            continue
        manifest["model"] = new_model
        new_blob = msgpack.packb(manifest, use_bin_type=True)
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE agents SET manifest = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?",
            (new_blob, agent_id),
        )
        changed += 1
        print(
            f"  update name={name} provider={OLD_PROVIDER}->{NEW_PROVIDER} "
            f"dropped_fields={list(FIELDS_TO_DROP)}"
        )
    conn.commit()
    print(f"done: {changed} agents migrated")
    conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"migration failed: {exc}\n")
        sys.exit(1)

from pathlib import Path

for name in AGENTS:
    p = Path(f'/opt/openfang/openfang-data/agents/{name}/agent.toml')
    lines = p.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
    new_lines = []
    in_model = False
    for line in lines:
        s = line.strip()
        if s == '[model]':
            in_model = True
            new_lines.append(line)
            continue
        if in_model and s.startswith('[') and s != '[model]':
            in_model = False
        if in_model:
            if s == 'provider = \"openai\"':
                new_lines.append('provider = \"vertex-ai\"\n')
                continue
            if s in ('api_key_env = \"OPENAI_API_KEY\"', 'base_url = \"http://litellm:4000/v1\"'):
                continue
        new_lines.append(line)
    p.write_text(''.join(new_lines))
    print(f'  {name}: updated')
PYEOF

echo

content.text:
## Bloqueador upstream encontrado, pero tenemos fix pequeño

**Bug**: el normalizador `normalize_schema_for_provider` de OpenFang v0.5.9 (y también v0.6.0) **no strippea todos los campos OpenAPI 3.0 que Vertex Gemini rechaza**:
- `deprecated` (OpenAPI 3)
- `readOnly` / `writeOnly`
- Vendor extensions `x-*` (como `x-google-enum-descriptions`)

Confirmé que los tools de MCP GitHub/Grafana traen estos campos. Vertex los rechaza con 400.

**Fix**: patch de ~5 líneas en `crates/openfang-types/src/tool.rs`. Agregar los campos a la lista de strip + catch-all para `x-*`. **Esto es fix legítimo de un bug upstream** — no es un fork divergente, se contribuye PR al mismo tiempo.

Tiempo adicional estimado: ~45 min (patch + `cargo build --release` + rebuild image + deploy + test). ¿Sigo?

Si preferís, alternativa rápida (~15 min): deshabilitar MCP GitHub/Grafana temporalmente para validar todo el resto del stack Vertex nativo, luego fix proper con el patch. Pero eso solo pospone el tema.

Mi recomendación: **patch + rebuild ahora, contribute PR después**. ¿Sigo?

Excelente — la propuesta de ChatGPT es el approach correcto. **Abandono el driver Vertex nativo** y construyo un adapter HTTP completo. Mismo patrón que el embedding-proxy pero extendido. Así NO toco código OpenFang.

Diagnóstico que ya tengo: `mcp-gke` y `mcp-logging` tienen esos campos en schemas. El adapter los sanitiza por request.

## Plan revisado — Vertex Adapter unificado

**Abandonar**:
- Driver Vertex nativo en OpenFang (revert provider vertex-ai en agent.toml + config.toml)
- gcloud-wrapper mount (ya no se usa si volvemos a provider=openai)

**Construir**: extender el `embedding-proxy` actual a `vertex-adapter` con:

| Endpoint | Función |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/embeddings` | (ya existe) OpenAI → Vertex text-embedding-005 |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | NUEVO. OpenAI → Vertex Gemini generateContent |
| Sanitize antes de enviar a Vertex | Strip `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly`, todo `x-*`, `$schema`, `$defs`, etc. de los tool schemas |
| OAuth rotation | Mismo token cache 50 min, common para ambos endpoints |

**Stack final**:
```
OpenFang (config: provider=openai, base_url=http://vertex-adapter:4001/v1)
  ↓
vertex-adapter (sanitize + OAuth rotation)
  ↓
Vertex AI us-east1 (Gemini 2.5 Flash + text-embedding-005)
```

### Ventajas vs LiteLLM
- **Superficie mínima** (~300 líneas vs millones)
- **Sin bugs cache_injector / set_verbose deprecated / retry amplification**
- **Sanitization schema built-in** (problema del bug que acabo de ver queda resuelto)
- **OAuth rotation propia**

### Costo real
- ~300 líneas Python adicionales (chat/completions + translation + sanitization)
- ~1.5-2h: implementación + test

¿Procedo? Si sí, arranco con revertir la parte Vertex-nativo y construir el adapter completo.

content.text:
Ultrathink profundo antes de ejecutar.

## Pivot crítico que cambia el diseño

**Vertex AI tiene endpoint OpenAI-compat nativo** (https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/multimodal/call-vertex-using-openai-library):

```
https://{REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/{PROJECT}/locations/{REGION}/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions
```

Acepta body OpenAI-format, auth con OAuth Bearer, **Google hace la translation internamente**.

### Esto reduce el adapter de 600-800 líneas a ~200

Mi adapter ya no tiene que:
- Transformar messages OpenAI → Gemini contents
- Mapear roles (`assistant` → `model`, `tool` → `user` con `functionResponse`)
- Reescribir `tool_calls` → `parts[{functionCall}]`
- Traducir response `candidates[0].content.parts` → `choices[0].message`

Solo tiene que:
1. **Rotar OAuth token** (ya hecho para embedding)
2. **Sanitize tool schemas** (strip `deprecated`, `x-*`, etc. recursively) antes de forward
3. **Passthrough HTTP** al endpoint OpenAI de Vertex
4. **Streaming passthrough** (chunked response)

### Consideraciones críticas antes de ejecutar

1. **Verificar empíricamente que el endpoint Vertex OpenAI existe para `us-east1`/`prod-apps-454414`** — algunos features son región-dependientes.

2. **Verificar si embeddings también está soportado en ese endpoint** — la doc menciona solo chat, puede ser chat-only.
   - Si SÍ: el adapter hace passthrough para ambos
   - Si NO: mantengo la translation custom del embedding-proxy para embeddings

3. **Streaming**: OpenFang probablemente usa `stream=true`. Mi adapter debe soportar chunked response (`requests.post(stream=True)` + yield chunks).

4. **Sanitization debe aplicar solo a `tools[*].function.parameters`**, no al body completo (los mensajes pueden legítimamente tener `x-*` data).

5. **Error passthrough**: 429/400/500 de Vertex deben llegar al cliente intactos para que OpenFang reintente según su lógica.

### Plan definitivo

**Fase 1 — Revert previos** (~10 min):
- `agent.toml` ×7: volver a `provider = "openai"` + `base_url = "http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1"` + `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"`
- `config.toml` `[default_model]`: volver a `provider = "openai"` + `base_url`
- `docker-compose.override.yml`: remover mount del `gcloud-wrapper.py`, remover env `VERTEX_AI_REGION/GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` del openfang service
- Restart openfang + verificar agents Running

**Fase 2 — Verificar Vertex OpenAI-compat endpoint** (~10 min, ANTES de escribir código):
- curl directo desde VM con OAuth token del metadata
- Test POST `/v1/beta1/.../endpoints/openapi/chat/completions` body OpenAI-shape
- Test POST `/v1/beta1/.../endpoints/openapi/embeddings` (si 200, passthrough; si 404, translate custom)

**Fase 3 — Extender embedding-proxy → adapter completo** (~60-90 min):
- Rename archivo proxy.py internamente (conceptual), service name sigue
- Add `/v1/chat/completions` con passthrough + sanitize + streaming
- Mantener `/v1/embeddings` (passthrough si Vertex OpenAI lo soporta, translate si no)
- Sanitize `STRIP_KEYS = {deprecated, readOnly, writeOnly, $schema, $defs, $ref, ..., x-* catch-all}`

**Fase 4 — Deploy + test** (~30 min):
- Build nueva image del adapter
- Replace container
- Ping test assistant + triage con tools reales

**Fase 5 — Cleanup + commit** (~20 min):
- Stop & remove litellm
- Archivar `litellm-config.yaml`, `cache_injector.py`
- Commit git con descripción completa

**Total**: 2.5 horas.

### Orden de ejecución

Arranco con Fase 2 primero (validación pre-código). Si el endpoint Vertex OpenAI no está disponible, todo el plan cambia.

input.command:
ssh openfang "
AGENTS='assistant triage-orchestrator gke-deep postgres-deep sentry-deep grafana-query github-query'

echo '=== Revert agent.toml model blocks ==='
sudo python3 <<'PYEOF'
from pathlib import Path

AGENTS = ['assistant', 'triage-orchestrator', 'gke-deep', 'postgres-deep', 'sentry-deep', 'grafana-query', 'github-query']

# After our last edit, the block looks like:
#   [model]
#   provider = \"vertex-ai\"
#   model = \"gemini-2.5-flash\"
#   max_tokens = ...
# We want it back to provider=openai, with api_key_env + base_url pointing at our adapter.

for name in AGENTS:
    p = Path(f'/opt/openfang-src/crates/openfang-kernel/../../../') # just dummy path, unused
    p = Path(f'/opt/openfang/openfang-data/agents/{name}/agent.toml')
    lines = p.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
    new_lines = []
    in_model = False
    inserted_fields = False
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        s = line.strip()
        if s == '[model]':
            in_model = True
            inserted_fields = False
            new_lines.append(line)
            continue
        if in_model and s.startswith('[') and s != '[model]':
            in_model = False
        if in_model and s == 'provider = \"vertex-ai\"':
            # Revert this line to openai and append the extra fields
            new_lines.append('provider = \"openai\"\n')
            continue
        if in_model and s == 'model = \"gemini-2.5-flash\"' and not inserted_fields:
            new_lines.append(line)
            new_lines.append('api_key_env = \"OPENAI_API_KEY\"\n')
            new_lines.append('base_url = \"http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1\"\n')
            inserted_fields = True
            continue
        new_lines.append(line)
    p.write_text(''.join(new_lines))
    print(f'  {name}: reverted')
PYEOF

echo
echo '=== Verify assistant model block ==='
sudo sed -n '37,45p' /opt/openfang/openfang-data/agents/assistant/agent.toml"

[default_model]
# LLM goes through the local vertex-adapter sidecar which speaks OpenAI
# protocol and forwards to Vertex AI's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The
# sidecar rotates OAuth tokens from the GCE metadata server and rewrites
# model names (gemini-2.5-flash → google/gemini-2.5-flash) on the way out.
# See apps/ai/files/embedding-proxy/ (service name kept for backwards compat

api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"
base_url    = "http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1"

[memory]
decay_rate  = 0.05
sqlite_path = "/data/openfang.db"
# Embedding goes through the same vertex-adapter sidecar, which translates
# OpenAI /v1/embeddings into Vertex :predict (the Vertex OpenAI-compat
# endpoint does not expose embeddings, only chat).
embedding_provider    = "openai"
embedding_model       = "text-embedding-3-small"
embedding_api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"

[provider_urls]
# Single sidecar for both LLM and embedding paths.
openai = "http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1"

# AUTO-GENERATED — TI-1415 (MCP Sentry) + TI-1417 (MCP Grafana) + TI-1428 (MCP GKE)
# Regenerado 2026-04-20
# TI-1416 (MCP Cloud Monitoring) deprecated — covered by mcp-grafana via stackdriver datasource.
# Backups: /opt/openfang.bak.20260420-185111 + docker-compose.override.yml.bak.*

services:
  # === Embedding sidecar — OpenAI-compat shim → Vertex text-embedding-005 ===
  # Replaces LiteLLM. Rotates OAuth tokens from the GCE metadata server on
  # every ~50 min and translates OpenAI /v1/embeddings into Vertex :predict.
  # OpenFang upstream has no Vertex embedding driver; this ~100-line sidecar
  # is the minimum surface to keep embeddings on Vertex without forking.
  openfang-embedding-proxy:
    image: openfang-embedding-proxy:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-embedding-proxy
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "4001"
    environment:
      VERTEX_PROJECT: prod-apps-454414
      VERTEX_REGION: us-east1
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:4001/health', timeout=3).read()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  mcp-sentry:
    image: openfang-mcp-sentry:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-sentry
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7002"
    environment:
      SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN}
      API_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${MCP_PROXY_SECRET}
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import socket; s=socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1',7002), timeout=2); s.close()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1428 — MCP GKE sidecar (replaces deprecated mcp-gcp-monitoring) ===
  mcp-gke:
    image: openfang-mcp-gke:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-gke
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7004"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:7004/healthz', timeout=3).read()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  mcp-grafana:
    image: grafana/mcp-grafana:latest
    container_name: openfang-mcp-grafana
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "8000"
    environment:
      GRAFANA_URL: https://observability.liftit.co
      GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN: ${GRAFANA_TOKEN}
    command:
      - -t
      - streamable-http
      - -address
      - 0.0.0.0:8000
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - /app/mcp-grafana
        - -h
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1430 — MCP Cloud Logging sidecar (persistent cross-service logs) ===
  mcp-logging:
    image: openfang-mcp-logging:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-logging
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "7005"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python3
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen(\"http://localhost:7005/healthz\", timeout=3).read()"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL


  # === TI-1431 — Slack Approver sidecar (interactive buttons + allowlist) ===
  openfang-slack-approver:
    image: openfang-slack-approver:0.1.1
    container_name: openfang-slack-approver

    environment:
      SLACK_APPROVER_BOT_TOKEN: ${SLACK_APPROVER_BOT_TOKEN}
      SLACK_APPROVER_APP_TOKEN: ${SLACK_APPROVER_APP_TOKEN}

      OPENFANG_API_BASE: http://openfang:50051
    volumes:
      - approver-state:/app/data
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1414 — MCP PostgreSQL sidecar (read-only queries) ===
  mcp-postgres:
    image: openfang-mcp-postgres:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped

      test:

      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - default
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL

  # === TI-1419 — MCP GitHub sidecar (Actions + repos + PRs, read-only) ===

    image: openfang-mcp-github:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-mcp-github
    restart: unless-stopped

    environment:
      GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}

  openfang-kuma-trigger:
    image: openfang-kuma-trigger:0.1.0
    container_name: openfang-kuma-trigger
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - openfang
    environment:

      KUMA_CHANNEL_ID: ${KUMA_CHANNEL_ID}

    volumes:

    networks:

        condition: service_healthy

input.content:
"""
Vertex adapter: OpenAI-compatible sidecar for OpenFang → Vertex AI.

Serves both endpoints OpenFang speaks (`/v1/chat/completions` and
`/v1/embeddings`) in OpenAI protocol, translates / forwards to Vertex AI
us-east1 (gemini-2.5-flash + text-embedding-005), and rotates OAuth
tokens from the GCE metadata server so we don't need LiteLLM or a
service-account key file.

Why this sidecar exists:
  1. OpenFang's Vertex AI driver shells out to `gcloud` for tokens — the
     container doesn't ship gcloud and rebuilding the image just to add
     it is a worse trade than a local shim.
  2. OpenFang's OpenAIEmbeddingDriver reads the API key once at startup
     and never rotates; Vertex OAuth tokens expire every hour. No
     upstream VertexEmbeddingDriver exists (PRs #997 open, #1052 closed).
  3. Running LiteLLM just for translation layered retries, cache hooks,
     and deprecated APIs on top of our hot path with no corresponding
     benefit. Replacing it with ~200 lines under our control is cheaper.

Request flow:
  /v1/chat/completions:
    OpenFang → this proxy → Vertex OpenAI-compat endpoint at
    {region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/.../endpoints/openapi/chat/completions
    Model name is rewritten to `google/<name>` so Vertex's endpoint
    accepts it. Vertex's endpoint already normalizes tool JSON Schema
    (strips fields like `deprecated` and `x-*` that generateContent
    rejects) so this proxy passes the body through untouched.
    Streaming responses are forwarded chunk-by-chunk.

  /v1/embeddings:
    OpenFang → this proxy → Vertex :predict (legacy Prediction API) at
    {region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/.../publishers/google/models/<model>:predict
    The Vertex OpenAI endpoint does not expose embeddings, so we keep
    the custom translation here.

Environment:
  VERTEX_PROJECT         required. GCP project id (e.g. prod-apps-454414)
  VERTEX_REGION          required. GCP region (e.g. us-east1)
  MODEL_MAP              optional. comma-separated openai-name:vertex-name pairs
                         (default: text-embedding-3-small:text-embedding-005)
  CHAT_MODEL_PREFIX      optional. prefix added to chat model names if not
                         already present. default "google/"
  LISTEN_PORT            optional. default 4001
  TOKEN_CACHE_SECONDS    optional. default 3000 (50 min; Vertex tokens expire at 60)
  TASK_TYPE              optional. default RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT (embeddings only)
  REQUEST_TIMEOUT        optional. default 120 (chat calls can be long)
"""
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import threading
import time
from urllib.error import URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

import requests
from flask import Flask, Response, jsonify, request, stream_with_context

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='{"ts":"%(asctime)s","level":"%(levelname)s","msg":%(message)s}',
)
log = logging.getLogger("vertex-adapter")


def _env_required(name: str) -> str:
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    if not value:
        sys.stderr.write(f"missing required env var: {name}\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return value


PROJECT = _env_required("VERTEX_PROJECT")
REGION = _env_required("VERTEX_REGION")
LISTEN_PORT = int(os.environ.get("LISTEN_PORT", "4001"))
TOKEN_CACHE_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("TOKEN_CACHE_SECONDS", "3000"))
TASK_TYPE = os.environ.get("TASK_TYPE", "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT")
CHAT_MODEL_PREFIX = os.environ.get("CHAT_MODEL_PREFIX", "google/")
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = int(os.environ.get("REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "120"))

DEFAULT_MODEL_MAP = "text-embedding-3-small:text-embedding-005"
MODEL_MAP = dict(
    pair.split(":", 1)
    for pair in os.environ.get("MODEL_MAP", DEFAULT_MODEL_MAP).split(",")
    if ":" in pair
)

METADATA_URL = (
    "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/"
    "instance/service-accounts/default/token"
)

VERTEX_OPENAI_BASE = (
    f"https://{REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/{PROJECT}/"
    f"locations/{REGION}/endpoints/openapi"
)
VERTEX_PREDICT_BASE = (
    f"https://{REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{PROJECT}/"
    f"locations/{REGION}/publishers/google/models"
)

    if not inputs or not isinstance(inputs, list) or not all(isinstance(s, str) for s in inputs):
        return jsonify({"error": {"message": "input must be string or list of strings"}}), 400

    vertex_url = (
        f"https://{REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{PROJECT}/"
        f"locations/{REGION}/publishers/google/models/{model_out}:predict"
    )
    vertex_body = {
        "instances": [{"content": s, "task_type": TASK_TYPE} for s in inputs],
    }

    # Retry once on 401 (token may have expired inside our cache window).
    last_response = None
    for attempt in (1, 2):
        token = get_token(force_refresh=(attempt == 2))
        t0 = time.time()
        last_response = requests.post(
            vertex_url,
            headers={
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
            },
            json=vertex_body,
            timeout=30,
        )
        dt_ms = int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)
        if last_response.status_code == 401 and attempt == 1:
            _logj("warning", "got_401_retrying_with_fresh_token")
            continue
        _logj(
            "info",
            "vertex_call",
            status=last_response.status_code,
            model=model_out,
            inputs=len(inputs),
            latency_ms=dt_ms,
        )
        break

    assert last_response is not None
    if last_response.status_code != 200:
        return (
            jsonify(
                {
                    "error": {
                        "message": last_response.text[:500],
                        "type": "upstream_error",
                        "code": last_response.status_code,
                    }
                }
            ),
            last_response.status_code,
        )

    predictions = last_response.json().get("predictions", [])
    data = []
    total_tokens = 0
    for i, pred in enumerate(predictions):
        emb = pred.get("embeddings", {})
        values = emb.get("values", [])
        data.append({"object": "embedding", "index": i, "embedding": values})
        total_tokens += emb.get("statistics", {}).get("token_count", 0) or 0

    return jsonify(
        {
            "object": "list",
            "data": data,
            "model": model_in,
            "usage": {"prompt_tokens": total_tokens, "total_tokens": total_tokens},
        }
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _logj(
        "info",
        "starting",
        project=PROJECT,
        region=REGION,
        port=LISTEN_PORT,
        model_map=MODEL_MAP,
        task_type=TASK_TYPE,
    )
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=LISTEN_PORT, threaded=True)

|---|---|

- `config.toml`: `[default_model]` apunta al adapter, `[heartbeat] default_timeout_secs=900` (workaround idle), `[provider_urls]` apunta al adapter

feat(apps/ai): TI-1432+ replace LiteLLM with vertex-adapter sidecar

Purpose-built OpenAI-compatible sidecar that replaces LiteLLM for the
Vertex AI integration path. Why:

  - OpenFang's native Vertex driver shells out to gcloud for OAuth
    tokens (not in the container image) and has no embedding driver
    (upstream PRs #997 open WIP, #1052 closed without merge — both
    target Gemini API consumer, not Vertex).
  - LiteLLM introduced bugs: cache_injector + tools = 403/400 cascade,
    deprecated set_verbose masking payload introspection, retry
    amplification contributing to TPM bursts on us-east1 PayGo pool.

Adapter responsibilities (~230 lines Python + Flask):

  - POST /v1/chat/completions → passthrough to Vertex's OpenAI-compat
    endpoint (/v1beta1/projects/{proj}/locations/{region}/endpoints/openapi/
    chat/completions). Rewrites model names (gemini-2.5-flash →
    google/gemini-2.5-flash). Streaming forwarded chunk-by-chunk.
    Vertex auto-sanitizes tool schemas, so OpenAPI fields like
    'deprecated' and 'x-*' extensions pass through without error.

  - POST /v1/embeddings → translate to Vertex :predict for
    text-embedding-005 (768-dim vectors). The OpenAI-compat endpoint
    returns 500 on embeddings for this region/project, so custom
    translation stays here.

  - OAuth bearer tokens fetched from GCE metadata server (cached 50 min;
    Vertex tokens expire at 60). The VM service account
    (compute-engine@prod-apps-454414) already has cloud-platform scope.
    No SA key file, no gcloud CLI needed.

VM-side changes (done out-of-band, not in this repo):

  - litellm container + image removed
  - litellm-config.yaml + cache_injector.py archived with timestamp
  - config.toml [default_model].base_url + 7 agents' manifest base_url
    repointed at http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1
  - docker-compose.override.yml replaces the litellm service with
    openfang-embedding-proxy (healthcheck, no-new-privileges, cap_drop:ALL)

Validated end-to-end:

  - chat_call 200 with full MCP tool schemas (github, gke, grafana,
    logging, postgres, sentry) — no schema rejection
  - embedding_call 200, 768 dims, consistent with previous LiteLLM
    → vertex_ai/text-embedding-005 mapping
  - OpenFang's native retry (3 attempts) absorbs transient 429s from
    the PayGo pool, as observed during smoke tests
  - All 7 agents remain Running post-cutover (assistant,
    triage-orchestrator, gke-deep, postgres-deep, sentry-deep,
    grafana-query, github-query)

Service name intentionally kept as openfang-embedding-proxy to avoid
DNS churn; internal docs call it the vertex-adapter. Rename can happen
in a follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

---
name: OpenFang Vertex Adapter + heartbeat workaround 2026-04-23
description: LiteLLM eliminado — sustituido por vertex-adapter sidecar (~230 líneas Python). OpenFang habla OpenAI protocol al adapter; adapter habla Vertex. Commit 7db3d46.
type: project
---

**SUPERSEDES operacionalmente**:
- `openfang-vertex-switch-2026-04-20.md` (LiteLLM era la solution, ya no corre)
- `openfang-ti1439-rollback-2026-04-22.md` (cache_injector bug resuelto eliminando LiteLLM)
- `vertex-gemini-429-root-cause-2026-04-22.md` (num_retries=1 en LiteLLM ya no aplica; OpenFang retry nativo=3 absorbe bursts)

## Arquitectura final

```
openfang kernel
  ├── LLM: provider=openai, base_url=http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1
  │     └── adapter → https://us-east1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/.../endpoints/openapi/chat/completions
  │         (passthrough + model rewrite gemini-2.5-flash → google/gemini-2.5-flash)
  └── Embedding: provider=openai, mismo base_url
        └── adapter → https://us-east1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/.../publishers/google/models/text-embedding-005:predict
            (translate OpenAI → Vertex :predict, 768 dims)
```

## Containers vivos (post-migración)

11 total, sin LiteLLM:
- `openfang` + `openfang-embedding-proxy` (adapter 0.2.0 — nombre service kept para no romper DNS refs)
- 6 MCPs: sentry, grafana, gke, logging, postgres, github
- `openfang-slack-approver`, `openfang-kuma-trigger`, `phoenix`

## OAuth flow

- Metadata server del VM (SA `compute-engine@prod-apps-454414`, scope `cloud-platform`)
- Adapter cachea token 50 min (Vertex expira a 60)
- Retry once on 401 (force refresh)

## Archivos en repo

Commit `7db3d46`:
- `apps/ai/files/embedding-proxy/proxy.py` — 230 líneas, Flask threaded
- `apps/ai/files/embedding-proxy/Dockerfile` — python:3.12-slim, user 65534
- `apps/ai/files/embedding-proxy/requirements.txt` — Flask 3.0.3 + requests 2.32.3

## Archivos en VM

- `/opt/openfang/embedding-proxy/` — source del sidecar (image built local)
- `/opt/openfang/config.toml` — `[default_model].base_url` + `[provider_urls].openai` apuntan al adapter + `[heartbeat].default_timeout_secs = 900`
- `/opt/openfang/docker-compose.override.yml` — sin service `litellm`, nuevo service `openfang-embedding-proxy`
- `/opt/openfang/openfang-data/agents/<name>/agent.toml` (×7) — `base_url` apunta al adapter
- Archivados con timestamp: `litellm-config.yaml.archived-*`, `cache_injector.py.archived-*`

## Heartbeat workaround (aplicado en esta sesión)

- `[heartbeat] default_timeout_secs = 900` en config.toml
- Razón: upstream bug issues #1089/#1090/#1102 (idle reactive agents marcados Crashed). Fix real pendiente upstream
- Ver log "Heartbeat monitor started (interval: 30s)" — interval sigue 30s, pero timeout ya no 180s
- Post-fix observado: 0 false-positives en 30 min de observación

## Bugs descartados / resueltos

- **cache_injector bug**: resuelto por eliminar LiteLLM
- **set_verbose deprecated warning**: resuelto por eliminar LiteLLM
- **No connected db error**: resuelto por migrar a Vertex adapter (era LiteLLM caching issue)
- **Tool schemas con `deprecated`/`x-*`**: Vertex OpenAI-compat endpoint auto-sanitiza. Adapter hace passthrough sin intervenir.

## Bugs que siguen (upstream)

- TPM 429 transients en pool us-east1 PayGo gemini-2.5-flash. OpenFang retry nativo (3 attempts) los absorbe pero bajo load alto puede cascade. Plan B (Provisioned Throughput) sigue en backlog.
- OpenFang Vertex driver nativo (vertex.rs) requiere gcloud subprocess — no apto para containers. No volvemos a ese path.
- OpenFang no tiene VertexEmbeddingDriver nativo (PRs #997 open, #1052 closed). El adapter lo reemplaza.

## Endpoint Vertex OpenAI compat — hallazgos

- **Chat**: FUNCIONA. Model name requiere prefijo `google/`. Auto-sanitiza schemas (acepta `deprecated`, `x-*` que Gemini native rechaza).
- **Embeddings**: devuelve HTTP 500 para nuestra región/proyecto. No usarlo; usar `:predict` clásico.
- URL base: `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/{project}/locations/{region}/endpoints/openapi`

## UUIDs de agents (persisten post-migración)

## 🎉 Sesión completada

### Stack final

11 containers, **sin LiteLLM**. OpenFang habla protocol OpenAI al sidecar `openfang-embedding-proxy:0.2.0` (el "vertex-adapter") que:

- **`/v1/chat/completions`**: passthrough a Vertex OpenAI-compat endpoint + model rewrite `google/*`
- **`/v1/embeddings`**: translate a Vertex `:predict` (text-embedding-005, 768 dims)
- **OAuth**: metadata server del VM (SA `compute-engine@prod-apps-454414`), cache 50 min

### Checks finales (últimos 5 min)

| Señal | Estado |
|---|---|
| Agents Running | 7/7 |
| Unresponsive warnings en logs | **0** (heartbeat workaround aplicado) |
| Adapter chat_call | 2×429 + 1×200 — retry nativo de OpenFang absorbe el burst |
| Adapter embedding_call | 200 ✓, ~90-115ms |

Los 429 del chat son el issue conocido del pool us-east1 PayGo. OpenFang retry=3 nativo los absorbe. No es nuevo, no es del adapter.

### Entregables

- **Commit `7db3d46`**: `feat(apps/ai): TI-1432+ replace LiteLLM with vertex-adapter sidecar` — 3 archivos, 322 líneas (proxy.py + Dockerfile + requirements.txt)
- **Memoria**: `openfang-vertex-adapter-2026-04-23.md` + entry en MEMORY.md con supersedes de los 3 memory files previos que quedaron stale
- **VM cleanup**: LiteLLM image eliminada (~1.7GB), `litellm-config.yaml` + `cache_injector.py` + `gcloud-wrapper.py` archivados/removidos
- **Config**: workaround heartbeat `default_timeout_secs=900` sigue aplicado

### Lo que resolvimos en esta sesión

1. **Bug idle heartbeat** (upstream #1089/#1090/#1102) → workaround config 180→900s
2. **Bug cache_injector + tools** → obsoleto (LiteLLM eliminado)
3. **Deprecation `set_verbose`** → obsoleto (LiteLLM eliminado)
4. **Retry amplification LiteLLM+OpenFang** → solo queda OpenFang retry=3
5. **Sovereignty concern embeddings** → todo tráfico va a Vertex us-east1, ningún consumer endpoint
6. **Schemas OpenAPI con `deprecated`/`x-*`** → Vertex OpenAI-compat auto-sanitiza, zero intervención

### Lo que NO resolvimos (continúa)

- **Pool PayGo 429 transients** bajo load — Provisioned Throughput sigue en backlog como Plan B
- **Rename service** `openfang-embedding-proxy` → `vertex-adapter` (solo cosmético, para siguiente sesión)

El commit NO está pusheado a origin (tu branch está 20 commits adelante ahora, vos decidís cuándo push).

content.text:
Excelente — la seguridad es una buena preocupación. Ultrathink antes de ejecutar.

## Plan estructurado

### Paso 0 — Security audit primero (para saber alcance)

1. **Bearer validation**: el adapter NO valida el `Authorization: Bearer` que recibe → cualquier container en la docker network puede abusar del Vertex billing. Debería validar.
2. **Metadata server exposure**: container tiene acceso. Unavoidable, mitigado con UID 65534 + cap_drop.
3. **Archivos archivados**: `litellm-config.yaml.archived-*` contiene `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` en texto plano. Debería eliminarse o moverse.
4. **Image residuos**: `python:3.12-slim` de la migration temporal, posibles imágenes intermedias.
5. **File permissions**: verificar ownership + mode.

### Paso 1 — Harden adapter con Bearer validation

Agregar env var `EXPECTED_BEARER` al adapter. Si llega distinto → 401. Default: si no está seteado, no valida (backwards compat). En prod siempre seteado.

### Paso 2 — Rename service

`openfang-embedding-proxy` → `vertex-adapter`. Cambios:
- `docker-compose.override.yml`: service name + container_name
- `config.toml`: `[default_model].base_url` + `[provider_urls].openai`
- 7 × `agent.toml`: `[model].base_url`
- `/opt/openfang/embedding-proxy/` → `/opt/openfang/vertex-adapter/`
- `apps/ai/files/embedding-proxy/` → `apps/ai/files/vertex-adapter/` en repo

Atomic deploy: update todo + `docker compose up --remove-orphans` + restart openfang.

### Paso 3 — Docker image cleanup

- `docker image prune -a --filter "until=24h"` (safe, solo no-referenced + antiguas)
- Review manual después

### Paso 4 — Archivos archivados seguros

- Mover `.archived-*` a `/opt/openfang/archive/` con perms 600 root-only
- O eliminar si ya no se necesitan (backup del backup)

### Paso 5 — Permissions audit

Arranco con el audit.

content.text:
## Audit completado

### Hallazgos

**Imágenes obsoletas a eliminar** (~10 imágenes, ~1.2GB liberables):
- `hello-world`, `alpine:latest`, `curlimages/curl:latest`, `ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy` (pre-pivot)
- `openfang-embedding-proxy:0.1.0` (actual es 0.2.0)
- `openfang-mcp-gcp-monitoring:0.1.0` (TI-1416 deprecated)
- `openfang-router:0.1.0` (descartado en TI-1433)
- `openfang-slack-approver:0.1.0` (actual es 0.1.1)

**Archivos sensibles**:
- `litellm-config.yaml.bak.pre-cache-*` tiene `master_key: sk-litellm-7976...` en plaintext. El master_key sigue siendo valor obsoleto (LiteLLM no corre) pero es buena práctica no dejar secrets residuales.
- 20+ archived/bak files en `/opt/openfang/` — residuo de semanas de iteración

**Security hardening containers**:
| Container | User | no-new-privileges | cap_drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| openfang (main) | **root!** | ❌ | ❌ |
| embedding-proxy | 65534 ✓ | ✓ | ALL ✓ |
| 6 MCPs + approver + trigger | non-root ✓ | ✓ | ALL ✓ |

El container `openfang` main corre como root sin hardening. Pre-existente (no lo tocamos hoy), pero vale anotarlo.

### Ejecución

Arranco S2 (Bearer validation en adapter) — cambio de código + rebuild. Luego S3 (rename).

# === vertex-adapter sidecar — OpenAI-compat shim → Vertex AI (replaces LiteLLM) ===
  # Serves /v1/chat/completions (passthrough to Vertex OpenAI-compat endpoint,
  # with model rewrite google/<name>) and /v1/embeddings (translate to Vertex
  # :predict, text-embedding-005, 768 dims). OAuth bearer rotation from the GCE
  # metadata server (cached 50 min). Enforces REQUIRED_BEARER to prevent other
  # containers on the shared docker network from abusing the VM SA's Vertex
  # quota.
  vertex-adapter:
    image: openfang-vertex-adapter:0.3.0
    container_name: openfang-vertex-adapter
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "4001"
    environment:

input.content:
"""
One-shot: rewrite the base_url inside each agent's manifest.model block
from the old embedding-proxy DNS to the renamed vertex-adapter DNS.

Run with openfang stopped to avoid SQLite write conflicts.
"""
import sqlite3
import sys

import msgpack

DB_PATH = "/data/openfang.db"
OLD_URL = "http://openfang-embedding-proxy:4001/v1"
NEW_URL = "http://vertex-adapter:4001/v1"


def main():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    rows = list(conn.execute("SELECT id, name, manifest FROM agents"))
    print(f"agents in DB: {len(rows)}")
    changed = 0
    for row in rows:
        manifest = msgpack.unpackb(row["manifest"], raw=False)
        model = manifest.get("model") or {}
        if not isinstance(model, dict):
            print(f"  skip {row['name']}: no model dict")
            continue
        if model.get("base_url") != OLD_URL:
            print(f"  skip {row['name']}: base_url={model.get('base_url')}")
            continue
        model["base_url"] = NEW_URL
        manifest["model"] = model
        new_blob = msgpack.packb(manifest, use_bin_type=True)
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE agents SET manifest = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?",
            (new_blob, row["id"]),
        )
        changed += 1
        print(f"  update {row['name']}: {OLD_URL} -> {NEW_URL}")
    conn.commit()
    print(f"done: {changed} agents migrated")
    conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"migration failed: {exc}\n")
        sys.exit(1)

for agent in assistant triage-orchestrator gke-deep postgres-deep sentry-deep grafana-query github-query; do
  sudo mv /opt/openfang/openfang-data/agents/$agent/agent.toml.bak* /opt/openfang/archive/ 2>/dev/null || true
  sudo mv /opt/openfang/openfang-data/agents/$agent/agent.toml.v3* /opt/openfang/archive/ 2>/dev/null || true
done
echo
echo "=== Contenido de archive/ ==="
sudo ls -la /opt/openfang/archive/ | head -40
echo "..."
sudo ls /opt/openfang/archive/ | wc -l
echo " total files in archive"
echo
echo "=== Verificar que /opt/openfang/ está limpio ==="
sudo ls -la /opt/openfang/ | grep -iE "bak|archived" | head -5 || echo "  clean"
echo
echo "=== Secrets leak check - ningún bak debe estar world-readable ==="
sudo find /opt/openfang/archive -type f -perm /004 2>/dev/null | head -10
echo "(empty = OK)"'

# apps/ai — AI Infrastructure VMs

## What This Module Does
Provisions VMs that host AI / LLM ops tooling for Liftit (OpenFang Hand orchestrator + Arize Phoenix observability stack). LLM inference se consume **vía Vertex AI Gemini 2.5 Flash regional us-east1** (managed, sin GPU propio). Slack Socket Mode + outbound HTTPS a Vertex AI no requieren ingress público.

> **HISTORICAL NOTE 2026-04-20:** Este módulo originalmente incluía `vllm.tf` con MIG regional T4 SPOT + ILB interno para self-hosted vLLM (Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ). Eliminado por inviabilidad de SPOT (preemption rate 2–12 min) + budget violation con on-demand. Pivote completo a Vertex AI managed. Ver `.planning/phases/07-openfang-hand-agente-llm-de-ops-e-incidentes/07-AI-SPEC.md` CHANGELOG.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `apps/ai`
- **Workspaces**: prod (only)

## VMs
| App | Env | Machine | Zone | Disk |
|-----|-----|---------|------|------|
| ai-infra-orchestrator | prod | e2-medium | us-east1-b | pd-ssd 50 GB |

## Resources Created
- VM via `tf-modules//vm` (Rocky Linux 9, CMEK encrypted boot disk, daily backup, deletion protection, alerting)
- Static internal IP, network tag `ssh` (no LB ingress)

## Bootstrap
The module does NOT install Docker / OpenFang / Phoenix. Provisioning of the container stack is performed manually over SSH after `terraform apply` (Option B per TI-1421 Parte 1 walking skeleton).

## Dependencies (remote state)
- `org/projects` (folders) — workspace `gen`
- `networking/vpc` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/kms` — workspace `sec`
- `iam/service-accounts` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/backup` — workspace `prod`

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Google `~> 7.0`

# apps/ai — AI Infrastructure VMs

## What This Module Does
Provisions the VM that hosts Liftit's AI / LLM ops stack:

- **OpenFang** kernel (agent OS) driving the Slack-facing ops assistant and a
  multi-agent correlation pipeline (TI-1433).
- **vertex-adapter** sidecar: OpenAI-compatible shim over Vertex AI (chat +
  embeddings). Replaces LiteLLM end-to-end.
- **MCP sidecars** (Sentry, Grafana, GKE, Cloud Logging, Postgres, GitHub) +
  two OpenFang "hand" sidecars (Slack approver, Kuma trigger).
- **Arize Phoenix** container for LLM observability (OTLP receiver, UI on
  loopback).

LLM inference runs through **Vertex AI Gemini 2.5 Flash regional us-east1**
(managed). Embeddings run through **Vertex AI text-embedding-005** (768 dims).
Slack Socket Mode + outbound HTTPS to Vertex — no ingress required.

> **HISTORICAL NOTE 2026-04-20:** Originally included `vllm.tf` with a T4 SPOT
> MIG + internal ILB for self-hosted vLLM (Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ). Dropped after SPOT
> preemption proved unworkable and on-demand blew the budget. Pivoted to
> Vertex AI managed. See
> `.planning/phases/07-openfang-hand-agente-llm-de-ops-e-incidentes/07-AI-SPEC.md`
> changelog.

> **HISTORICAL NOTE 2026-04-23:** LiteLLM was used as the OpenAI→Vertex
> translation layer through TI-1432 cutover. Removed in favour of the
> in-repo `vertex-adapter` sidecar after a chain of LiteLLM-specific
> bugs (cache_injector + tools cascade, deprecated `set_verbose`, retry
> amplification worsening the us-east1 PayGo TPM burst). OpenFang's own
> Vertex driver was not a fit either: it shells out to `gcloud` for
> tokens (not in the container image) and has no embedding driver
> upstream (PRs #997 open, #1052 closed without merge — both target
> Gemini API consumer, not Vertex). The adapter is ~250 lines.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `apps/ai`
- **Workspaces**: prod (only)

## VM
| App | Env | Machine | Zone | Disk |
|-----|-----|---------|------|------|
| ai-infra-orchestrator | prod | e2-medium | us-east1-b | pd-ssd 50 GB |

Terraform creates the VM (Rocky Linux 9, CMEK boot disk, daily backup,
deletion protection, alerting), a static internal IP, and network tag `ssh`.
No public LB. Container provisioning is manual over SSH — Terraform only owns
the host.

## Container stack (deployed to the VM)

All services run under docker compose. Source for everything we build is
under `apps/ai/files/` in this repo.

| Container | Image | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `openfang` | `openfang-local:0.5.9` (built from upstream) | Agent kernel. 7 agents (assistant, triage-orchestrator, gke-deep, postgres-deep, sentry-deep, grafana-query, github-query). |
| `openfang-vertex-adapter` | `openfang-vertex-adapter:0.3.0` (built from `files/vertex-adapter/`) | OpenAI-compat shim for Vertex AI. Enforces shared bearer auth. |
| `openfang-mcp-sentry` | built from `files/mcp-sentry/` | Sentry issues + events (read-only) |
| `openfang-mcp-grafana` | `grafana/mcp-grafana:latest` (third-party) | Grafana dashboards + PromQL/LogQL |
| `openfang-mcp-gke` | built from `files/mcp-gke/` | K8s read + patch (patch gated by approval) |
| `openfang-mcp-logging` | built from `files/mcp-logging/` | Cloud Logging queries |
| `openfang-mcp-postgres` | built from `files/mcp-postgres/` | Read-only SQL to prod `ebdb` |
| `openfang-mcp-github` | built from `files/mcp-github/` (wraps `ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server`) | Actions/repos/PRs (read-only) |
| `openfang-slack-approver` | built from `files/openfang-slack-approver/` | Interactive approval buttons + allowlist |
| `openfang-kuma-trigger` | built from `files/openfang-kuma-trigger/` | Polls Slack Kuma channel, fires agent on DOWN events |
| `phoenix` | `arizephoenix/phoenix:14.8.0` | LLM observability (OTLP receiver, UI loopback-only) |

## How the LLM path works

```
OpenFang kernel  ──OpenAI protocol──►  openfang-vertex-adapter
                                       │
     ┌─── /v1/chat/completions         ├── OAuth token from GCE metadata
     │       passthrough (model        │   (SA: compute-engine@prod-apps-454414,
     │       rewrite gemini-2.5-flash  │    scope cloud-platform; cached 50 min)
     │       → google/gemini-2.5-flash)│
     │                                 ▼
     │                                 Vertex AI us-east1
     │                                 /v1beta1/.../endpoints/openapi/chat/completions
     │                                 (Google's OpenAI-compat endpoint —
     │                                  auto-sanitizes tool schemas, so OpenAPI
     │                                  fields like `deprecated` and `x-*`
     │                                  extensions that Gemini native rejects
     │                                  pass through untouched)
     │
     └─── /v1/embeddings               ├── same OAuth token
             translate OpenAI →        │
             Vertex :predict           │
                                       ▼
                                       Vertex AI us-east1
                                       /v1/.../publishers/google/models/
                                       text-embedding-005:predict
                                       (The OpenAI-compat endpoint returns 500
                                        on embeddings for our region/project,
                                        so we keep the translation custom.)
```

Auth enforcement: the adapter reads `REQUIRED_BEARER` from env; OpenFang sends
`Authorization: Bearer $VERTEX_ADAPTER_BEARER` (sourced from the VM `.env`).
Bearer mismatch → 401. This prevents other containers on the shared docker
network from free-riding on the VM SA's Vertex quota.

## Security posture (per-container)

| Container | User | no-new-privileges | cap_drop | Ingress |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| openfang | root | ❌ | ❌ | loopback 4200, 50051 |
| vertex-adapter | 65534 | ✅ | ALL | docker network only (expose 4001) |
| 6 MCPs | non-root | ✅ | ALL | docker network only |
| slack-approver | non-root | ✅ | ALL | docker network only |
| kuma-trigger | non-root | ✅ | ALL | docker network only |
| phoenix | default | default | default | loopback 6006, 4317 |

openfang itself running as root with no cap_drop is an upstream constraint
(kernel binary signals on start). Track if future OpenFang versions allow
non-root runtime.

## On-VM config layout (under `/opt/openfang/`)

- `config.toml` — kernel config (default_model + memory + MCP servers +
  approval policy + heartbeat). `base_url` on both `[default_model]` and
  `[provider_urls].openai` points at the adapter.
- `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.override.yml` — stack definition.
- `.env` — secrets (Slack tokens, Grafana token, Postgres URL, GitHub PAT,
  approver allowlist, `VERTEX_ADAPTER_BEARER`). Mode 600.
- `openfang-data/` — SQLite DB (`openfang.db`, holds the agent manifests
  including `[model].base_url`), per-agent directories with `agent.toml`,
  skill files (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`).
- `vertex-adapter/` — Dockerfile + proxy.py + requirements.txt used to
  build the image locally.
- `mcp-*/`, `openfang-*/` — source for each locally-built sidecar.
- `archive/` — mode 700, holds timestamped backups of config.toml,
  docker-compose.override.yml, and the agents' manifests from each
  deploy. All files inside are mode 600.

## Outstanding workarounds

- `[heartbeat] default_timeout_secs = 900` in `config.toml`. OpenFang marks
  reactive agents as `Crashed` after 180 s of idle (upstream bug
  #1089 / #1090 / #1102 — open at time of writing). Bumping the timeout to
  15 min suppresses the false positives until upstream lands the fix.

## Dependencies (remote state)
- `org/projects` (folders) — workspace `gen`
- `networking/vpc` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/kms` — workspace `sec`
- `iam/service-accounts` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/backup` — workspace `prod`

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Google `~> 7.0`

# apps/ai — AI Infrastructure VMs

## What This Module Does
Provisions VMs that host AI / LLM ops tooling for Liftit (OpenFang Hand orchestrator + Arize Phoenix observability stack). LLM inference se consume **vía Vertex AI Gemini 2.5 Flash regional us-east1** (managed, sin GPU propio). Slack Socket Mode + outbound HTTPS a Vertex AI no requieren ingress público.

> **HISTORICAL NOTE 2026-04-20:** Este módulo originalmente incluía `vllm.tf` con MIG regional T4 SPOT + ILB interno para self-hosted vLLM (Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ). Eliminado por inviabilidad de SPOT (preemption rate 2–12 min) + budget violation con on-demand. Pivote completo a Vertex AI managed. Ver `.planning/phases/07-openfang-hand-agente-llm-de-ops-e-incidentes/07-AI-SPEC.md` CHANGELOG.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `apps/ai`
- **Workspaces**: prod (only)

## VMs
| App | Env | Machine | Zone | Disk |
|-----|-----|---------|------|------|
| ai-infra-orchestrator | prod | e2-medium | us-east1-b | pd-ssd 50 GB |

## Resources Created
- VM via `tf-modules//vm` (Rocky Linux 9, CMEK encrypted boot disk, daily backup, deletion protection, alerting)
- Static internal IP, network tag `ssh` (no LB ingress)

## Bootstrap
The module does NOT install Docker / OpenFang / Phoenix. Provisioning of the container stack is performed manually over SSH after `terraform apply` (Option B per TI-1421 Parte 1 walking skeleton).

## Dependencies (remote state)
- `org/projects` (folders) — workspace `gen`
- `networking/vpc` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/kms` — workspace `sec`
- `iam/service-accounts` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/backup` — workspace `prod`

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Google `~> 7.0`

Push exitoso: `c593db3..8458bbd` → origin/master. 21 commits publicados.

## Cómo probar que todo funciona

Armé la guía en niveles — arriba lo más barato, abajo lo más completo. Cada comando es copy-paste.

### Nivel 1 — Smoke tests del adapter (60 segundos)

Estos validan el adapter aislado. Si fallan, problema es del sidecar, no de OpenFang.

```bash
# Desde cualquier lado — por DNS docker (dentro de openfang VM)
ssh openfang 'docker exec openfang python3 -c "
import json
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
BEARER = open(\"/data/.env\").read() if False else \"\"
# Leer bearer del env del container
import os
BEARER = os.environ[\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"]
# Chat test
req = Request(\"http://vertex-adapter:4001/v1/chat/completions\",
    data=json.dumps({\"model\":\"gemini-2.5-flash\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"say OK\"}]}).encode(),
    headers={\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\",\"Authorization\":f\"Bearer {BEARER}\"})
r = json.load(urlopen(req, timeout=30))
print(\"chat:\", r[\"choices\"][0][\"message\"][\"content\"])
# Embedding test
req = Request(\"http://vertex-adapter:4001/v1/embeddings\",
    data=json.dumps({\"model\":\"text-embedding-3-small\",\"input\":\"test\"}).encode(),
    headers={\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\",\"Authorization\":f\"Bearer {BEARER}\"})
r = json.load(urlopen(req, timeout=30))
print(\"embed dims:\", len(r[\"data\"][0][\"embedding\"]))
"'
```

**Esperado**: `chat: OK` o similar, `embed dims: 1536` *(el sidecar devuelve 1536 nominales al cliente pero los valores reales son 768 de Vertex — OpenFang no valida, funciona)*. Wait — en realidad vimos 768 en los tests anteriores. Esto depende de `infer_dimensions`: el driver de OpenFang declara 1536 para `text-embedding-3-small` pero el array real viene 768. No afecta operación.

### Nivel 2 — Seguridad: bearer incorrecto → 401

```bash
ssh openfang 'docker exec openfang python3 -c "
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from urllib.error import HTTPError
import json
try:
    req = Request(\"http://vertex-adapter:4001/v1/chat/completions\",
        data=json.dumps({\"model\":\"gemini-2.5-flash\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}).encode(),
        headers={\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\",\"Authorization\":\"Bearer WRONG\"})
    urlopen(req, timeout=5)
    print(\"FAIL: bearer inválido pasó\")
except HTTPError as e:
    print(f\"OK: rechazado con {e.code}\")
"'
```

**Esperado**: `OK: rechazado con 401`.

### Nivel 3 — Ping a cada uno de los 7 agents via CLI

Cada agent con su UUID. Si falla uno específico, puede ser su manifest o su MCP.

```bash
ssh openfang '
UUIDS="
assistant:c473515d-f282-4c54-92a9-f20016440a2c
triage-orchestrator:36e7f972-8a75-4735-bb2b-af500885ddde
gke-deep:ecfb2971-c04c-46e3-ae00-66aaa2f93f97
postgres-deep:349f0b75-23b6-435c-adff-d1a507a471b6
sentry-deep:85010449-bc57-4026-b5d7-079cbba7ea6f
grafana-query:6019878d-82b7-4730-8e06-6767a93a4c52
github-query:681242f3-c6fa-4312-b039-f24f636fa0b8
"
for pair in $UUIDS; do
  name=$(echo $pair | cut -d: -f1)
  uuid=$(echo $pair | cut -d: -f2)
  echo "=== $name ==="
  timeout 60 docker exec openfang openfang message $uuid "ping responde en 3 palabras" --json 2>&1 | head -3
  echo
done'
```

**Esperado**: cada uno con `"cost_usd":...`, `"response":"..."` (no `"error"`).

### Nivel 4 — Tests end-to-end de features reales

**4a. Consulta real a Sentry** (vía assistant):
```bash
ssh openfang 'docker exec openfang openfang message c473515d-f282-4c54-92a9-f20016440a2c "listá los 3 errores Sentry más recientes en prod-apps-454414 proyecto core" --json 2>&1 | head -15'
```
Debería invocar `mcp_sentry_list_issues`.

**4b. Consulta Grafana** (vía grafana-query):
```bash
ssh openfang 'docker exec openfang openfang message 6019878d-82b7-4730-8e06-6767a93a4c52 "qué dashboards Grafana existen sobre linkerd" --json 2>&1 | head -15'
```

**4c. Consulta GKE** (vía gke-deep):
```bash
ssh openfang 'docker exec openfang openfang message ecfb2971-c04c-46e3-ae00-66aaa2f93f97 "estado del deployment finance-domain en lms-gke-prod" --json 2>&1 | head -20'
```

**4d. Approval flow** (patch gated — **NO ejecutar en prod sin coordinación**):
- Pedirle al assistant que reinicie algún deployment dev
- Verificar que aparece mensaje en `#infrastructure-approvals` con botones Approve/Reject
- Verificar que approver allowlist te permite aprobar
- Timeout 120s si no se aprueba

### Nivel 5 — Slack real (la prueba que más importa)

Desde tu cliente Slack:
1. **DM al bot** o **mention `@openfang-assistant ...`** en un canal donde está invitado
2. Prueba mensajes tipo:
   - `qué alertas están abiertas ahora`
   - `estado de finance-domain`
   - `último deploy de core-api`
3. Verificar que responde en < 60s

**Si querés confirmar que pasa por el adapter, mientras mandás el mention** corré en otra terminal:
```bash
ssh openfang 'docker logs -f openfang-vertex-adapter --since 10s' &
# Mandás el mention en Slack
# Deberías ver chat_call 200 con model=google/gemini-2.5-flash
```

### Nivel 6 — Monitoreo continuo

Una sola vista de todo:
```bash
ssh openfang 'docker logs -f openfang-vertex-adapter 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered -E "chat_call|embedding_call|auth_rejected"'
```
Podés dejarlo corriendo durante el día. Cualquier 429 (pool PayGo burst) aparecerá ahí. Si ves `auth_rejected` significa que alguien (o algún container) está intentando abusar.

### Nivel 7 — Kuma trigger (automation real)

`openfang-kuma-trigger` polls el canal Slack Kuma cada 30s buscando `DOWN`. Para probarlo:
- Forzar un DOWN en un endpoint monitoreado por Kuma
- Verificar que aparece reacción automática del bot en el canal + mensaje en un thread

(Esta es la prueba más cara de ejecutar — hacer solo si querés validar esa integración específica.)

### Rollback rápido (por si algo rompe)

Si ves fallos consistentes, rollback es 2 minutos. Todo está en `/opt/openfang/archive/` mode 600. Te doy los comandos exactos si los necesitás.

**Mi recomendación de orden**: Nivel 1 → 2 → 3 (5 min total). Si los 3 pasan, hacer Nivel 5 (Slack real). Los demás son opcionales según qué te interese validar.

**Excelente — end-to-end funcionando al 100%.** 🎉

El flujo completo pasó:
```
Slack Events API → OpenFang kernel → vertex-adapter → Vertex AI → response → Slack
```

Y el agent invocó `mcp_postgres_query` correctamente (detectó schema real, no inventó data).

## Dos observaciones

### 1. La migración es exitosa en prod real
- Slack Socket Mode funciona
- El adapter transportó el chat + los tool schemas (postgres MCP)
- Bearer validation no rechazó (los dos containers comparten el mismo secret correctamente)
- Response en español, latencia aceptable para el user

### 2. Hay un tema **no relacionado al adapter** que vale anotar

El agent reportó: *"La columna `waiting` no existe en `pg_stat_activity`"*. Es verdad — PostgreSQL 9.6+ reemplazó `waiting` (bool) por `wait_event_type` + `wait_event` (más granular).

El agent intentó una query con `waiting`, falló, y reportó "no hay bloqueos". **Falso negativo potencial**: podría haber bloqueos reales y el agent los perdió.

La query correcta para detectar bloqueos en PG modernas:
```sql
SELECT pid, wait_event_type, wait_event, state, query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE wait_event_type = 'Lock' AND state != 'idle';
```

Esto es un gap del **skill `pg-health-playbook`** o del **system prompt de postgres-deep**, no del adapter. Vale para un follow-up: actualizar el skill para PG 9.6+ (y probablemente ya estás en PG 14+ en prod).

¿Querés que ajuste el skill ahora o lo dejamos para después? Puedo mirar `apps/ai/files/skills/pg-health-playbook/SKILL.md` y agregar ejemplos de queries que compensen por versiones modernas de PG.

description: Postgres 17 (ebdb prod) health diagnosis. Collaboration mode, read-only.

# Postgres Health (PG 17)

Invocado con `evidence: "<error>"` desde gke-deep/grafana-query/assistant.
Ejecutar via `mcp_postgres_query` (read-only user `claude_readonly`). Nunca escribir.

## Version note
Target: **PostgreSQL 17** (prod `ebdb`). **NO USAR** la columna `waiting` de
`pg_stat_activity` — fue eliminada en PG 9.6. Hoy se usa
`wait_event_type IS NOT NULL` + `pg_blocking_pids(pid)`.

## Queries estándar (copy-paste, PG 17)

### 1. Distribución de conexiones
```sql
SELECT state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE backend_type = 'client backend'
GROUP BY state ORDER BY count DESC;
```

### 2. Sesiones activas + esperas
```sql
SELECT pid, usename, application_name, state,
       wait_event_type, wait_event,
       now() - query_start AS dur, LEFT(query, 120) AS q
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state != 'idle' AND backend_type = 'client backend'
ORDER BY dur DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20;
```

### 3. Bloqueos reales (usa `pg_blocking_pids`, no `waiting`)
```sql
SELECT blocked.pid AS blocked_pid,
       blocked.usename AS blocked_user,
       LEFT(blocked.query, 80) AS blocked_query,
       blocking.pid AS blocking_pid,
       blocking.usename AS blocking_user,
       LEFT(blocking.query, 80) AS blocking_query,
       now() - blocked.query_start AS blocked_for
FROM pg_stat_activity blocked
JOIN pg_stat_activity blocking
  ON blocking.pid = ANY(pg_blocking_pids(blocked.pid))
WHERE blocked.wait_event_type = 'Lock'
ORDER BY blocked_for DESC LIMIT 20;
```

Si la query devuelve 0 filas → **no hay bloqueos activos en este instante**.
Reportarlo así literal, no inferir "no hay problema".

### 4. Idle-in-transaction leaks (txn abiertos sin actividad)
```sql
SELECT pid, usename, application_name,
       now() - state_change AS idle_for, LEFT(query, 120)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state = 'idle in transaction'
  AND now() - state_change > interval '1 minute'
ORDER BY idle_for DESC LIMIT 10;
```

### 5. Replication lag (si hay standby)
```sql
SELECT client_addr, application_name, state, sync_state,
       pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), replay_lsn) AS lag_bytes,
       now() - reply_time AS lag_time
FROM pg_stat_replication;
```

### 6. Cache hit ratio
```sql
SELECT sum(blks_hit)::float / NULLIF(sum(blks_hit) + sum(blks_read), 0) AS hit_ratio
FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname NOT IN ('template0','template1');
```
Sano ≥ 0.99. Bajo de 0.95 sostenido → working set > shared_buffers.

### 7. Top slow queries (requiere `pg_stat_statements`)
```sql
SELECT LEFT(query, 100) AS q, calls,
       round(mean_exec_time::numeric, 2) AS avg_ms,
       round(total_exec_time::numeric, 0) AS total_ms
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC LIMIT 15;
```
Si la extensión no está: reportarlo y sugerir `CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements;`.

## Correlación evidence → causa

| Evidence | Diagnosis | Suggested action |
|---|---|---|
| `too many connections` | pool exhausted | (2) + (4) — matar idle-in-tx; revisar pool app |
| `connection refused` | DB down / firewall | Escalar; validar Cloud SQL + firewall |
| `statement_timeout` | slow query | (7) + `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`; falta índice |
| `deadlock detected` | lock conflict | (3) — reportar pid-pairs + orden de adquisición |
| `canceling statement due to lock timeout` | lock contention | (3) + identify long-running tx |
| `idle in transaction` count ↑ | txn leak app-side | (4); escalar a owner del service |
| Replication lag > 100MB | standby detrás | (5) + métrica Cloud SQL; buscar long-running en primary |
| Cache hit < 0.95 | I/O pressure | (6) + `EXPLAIN (BUFFERS)`; tune shared_buffers o indices |

## Output format

```
{
  db_health_summary: {
    connections: {active, idle, idle_in_tx},
    blocked_sessions: <count>,
    slow_top_3: [{query, avg_ms, calls}, ...],
    replication_lag_bytes: <n or null>,
    cache_hit_ratio: <0.0-1.0>
  },
  root_cause: "<one sentence>",
  suggested_action: "<what owner should do>"
}
```

Si alguna query falla, reportar el error literal (nunca inventar data).

## Cómo re-testar

Retesta el mismo mention que antes:

> `@Monitoreo_integraciones valida si hay bloqueos en la db de producción`

**Diferencias esperadas con el skill nuevo**:

1. **No debe usar `waiting`** — el skill ahora lo prohíbe explícitamente y provee la query correcta (#3 usa `pg_blocking_pids` + `wait_event_type = 'Lock'`).
2. **Respuesta más rica**: debería reportar count de sesiones bloqueadas, y si hay ≥1, listar pares `blocked_pid / blocking_pid` con la query truncada.
3. **Si realmente no hay bloqueos**: reportará *"0 sesiones bloqueadas en este instante"* literal — no *"no pude usar el filtro"*.

### Otras mentions útiles para validar el skill expandido

- `@Monitoreo_integraciones cuántas conexiones idle-in-transaction hay en prod` → dispara query #4
- `@Monitoreo_integraciones cuál es el cache hit ratio de ebdb` → dispara query #6
- `@Monitoreo_integraciones cuáles son las 5 queries más lentas en prod` → dispara query #7 (o reporta si `pg_stat_statements` no está)
- `@Monitoreo_integraciones hay replication lag en ebdb` → dispara query #5

### Mientras probás, monitor en otra terminal

```bash
ssh openfang 'docker logs -f openfang-vertex-adapter --since 10s 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered -E "chat_call|auth_rejected"'

content.content:
# PostgreSQL Blocking Lock Detection Queries

Based on the wiki content, here are the key SQL queries:

## Simple Blocking Detection

The wiki recommends starting with basic `pg_locks` inspection:

```sql
select relation::regclass, * from pg_locks where not granted;
```

## Detailed Blocking Query

The comprehensive query for identifying blocked and blocking processes:

```sql
SELECT blocked_locks.pid AS blocked_pid,
       blocked_activity.usename AS blocked_user,
       blocking_locks.pid AS blocking_pid,
       blocking_activity.usename AS blocking_user,
       blocked_activity.query AS blocked_statement,
       blocking_activity.query AS current_statement_in_blocking_process
FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked_locks
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocked_activity ON blocked_activity.pid = blocked_locks.pid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_locks blocking_locks ON blocking_locks.locktype = blocked_locks.locktype
AND blocking_locks.database IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.database
AND blocking_locks.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.relation
AND blocking_locks.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.page
AND blocking_locks.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.tuple
AND blocking_locks.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.virtualxid
AND blocking_locks.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.transactionid
AND blocking_locks.classid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.classid
AND blocking_locks.objid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objid
AND blocking_locks.objsubid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objsubid
AND blocking_locks.pid != blocked_locks.pid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocking_activity ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking_locks.pid
WHERE NOT blocked_locks.granted;
```

**Note:** The wiki cautions this query "still has some correctness issues," particularly on PostgreSQL 9.6.
